raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

With `--grammar-backend llguidance`, finishing a tool call gives HTTP 500. A legacy structural tag spells special tokens such as `</tool_call>` as forced text. llguidance tokenizes that text into the special token, allows only that token, and then rejects it:

```text
Grammar accept_token failed: Parser Error: token "�[151658]" doesn't satisfy the grammar; forced bytes: got '<'; applying 'ÿ'
```

This reaches `hermes`, `qwen`, `qwen25`, `trinity`, `apertus2509`, `deepseekv3` and `deepseekv31` on tokenizers that define these tokens as special.

The Rust schema for one tool has no `"type": "object"`, so named and one-tool `required` calls accept `["abc"]`. #48116 fixes the Python copy, so this PR leaves it.

## Modifications

The llguidance backend now writes each structure as a Lark grammar that references special tokens by ID. The Rust schema now sets `"type": "object"`.

A text trigger now fails at 667 tools, where main works up to 1990. Among served parsers, only `mistral` has one, and a user `structural_tag` can use one. The compile limit also falls for both trigger kinds.

This PR does not fix:

- `--reasoning-parser` (#33061, #25700). Merge this first: at `d59bb5520d`, #33061 alone killed the server on the first finished call, and #33061 with this fix did not.
- `at_least_one`, which llguidance ignores on legacy tags. Most no-call responses are empty: the mask blocks `<think>`, the model's first choice, so the model can stop at once.
- `mistral`, native tags, and `glm47` with non-strict tools (see the table).

## Accuracy Tests

The model forward does not change, so I ran no accuracy eval. I served `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` on one B200 from main `1ef3335da1` and from this diff merged with it, with `--grammar-backend llguidance`. I omitted the cookbook's `--reasoning-parser qwen3`, which llguidance cannot serve on main.

| Check (parser rows: 24 requests, temperature 0.8, `max_tokens` 128) | Main | This diff |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--tool-call-parser qwen25`, named | 4 HTTP 500, 20 no call | 4 with calls, 20 no call |
| `--tool-call-parser qwen25`, `required` | 3 HTTP 500, 21 no call | 5 with calls, 19 no call |
| `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`, `--tool-call-parser llama3`, one tool, named | 16 arrays of non-objects, 6 with calls, 2 stopped at `max_tokens` | 23 with calls, 1 stopped at `max_tokens` |
| `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1`, `--tool-call-parser llama3`, one tool, `required` | 12 arrays of non-objects, 8 with calls, 4 stopped at `max_tokens` | 24 with calls |
| No parser, named (Python schema, left to #48116) | 17 arrays of non-objects, 5 arrays of calls, 2 stopped at `max_tokens` | 19, 3 and 2 in the same order. With #48116 merged: 24 arrays of calls |
| `--tool-call-parser deepseekv32` (native tag), named, `required`, strict `auto` (12 requests) | HTTP 400 `Failed to compile structural_tag grammar` | Same |
| User `structural_tag` with trigger `<fn=`, small schema, 667 tools, 8 requests | No failure. A CPU walk finishes a call at 1990 tools | HTTP 500 `Current row has 2001 items; max is 2000` when a call starts. A CPU walk finishes a call at 666 tools |
| The same tag, 1990 tools, 8 requests | No failure | All HTTP 400 `panic: assertion failed: grammar.symbols.len() < u16::MAX as usize - 10` |
| Row limit, special-token trigger | About 665 tools | About 665 tools |
| Most tools that compile, 30 `anyOf` properties for each tool, special-token and text trigger | 374 and 378 | 366 and 372 |
| Most tools that compile, one string property, special-token and text trigger | About 2045 and 2180 | About 1820 and 1985 |
| Most tools that compile, one string property with `additionalProperties: false`, special-token and text trigger | About 4365 and 5040 | About 3445 and 4090 |
| Median of five CPU compiles, one string property with `additionalProperties: false`, 2 and 200 tools | 1.4 and 11.9 ms | 2.2 and 121.0 ms |
| Median of five CPU compiles, one string property without it, 2 and 200 tools | 1.6 and 31.8 ms | 2.5 and 146.0 ms |
| Mask fill in free text, 50 tools | 21 us | 20 us |
| CPU walk of one call in each tokenizer's own tokens: `hermes`, `qwen`, `qwen25`, `trinity` on Qwen3-0.6B and GLM-5.3, `hermes`, `qwen25` on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and MiniMax-M3, `deepseekv3`, `deepseekv31` on DeepSeek-V3.2, `apertus2509` on Apertus-8B-Instruct-2509 | Fails with the error above | Finishes |
| CPU walk, `mistral` on Mistral-7B-v0.3 and pixtral-12b | The mask blocks `[TOOL_CALLS]` at the first token | Same |
| Compile of native `qwen3_coder` and `deepseekv4` tags | Fails | Same |
| `glm47` on GLM-5.3, non-strict tools (`full_assistant_ebnf`), first mask fill | `Too many items (limit 50000; mask)` | Same |
| Backend on the Kimi-K3 tokenizer | `Only fast tokenizers are supported` | Same |

The new tests fail on main. The constrained and function-call unit tests, `sglang-processor` tool tests and Linux workspace clippy found no issue. In `pre-commit`, only clippy failed, because `sglang-server` cannot build on macOS.

I did not run GLM, DeepSeek, Mistral or MiniMax weights, the disaggregated, speculative or NPU paths, the DeepSeek-V4.1 tokenizer (not in the lab), or CI.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

A compile on a cache miss takes longer, and mask fill does not change (see the table).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

detail.title: [Fix] llguidance: Accept special tokens in tool tags

files.patch:
@@ -15,6 +15,7 @@
 
 import json
 import logging
+import re
 from functools import cache
 from typing import Iterable, List, NamedTuple, Optional, Tuple, Union
 
@@ -300,29 +301,53 @@ def dispatch_ebnf(self, key_string: str) -> BaseGrammarObject:
             logger.error(f"Hit invalid ebnf: {key_string=}, {e=}")
             return InvalidGrammarObject(str(e))
 
+    def _lark_literal(self, text: str) -> str:
+        """Spell ``text`` in Lark, with its special tokens as token references.
+
+        llguidance tokenizes forced text into any special token it spells, then
+        rejects that token because special tokens never match text bytes.
+        """
+        tokenizer = self.llguidance_tokenizer
+        special_tokens = {
+            tokenizer.decode_str([token]): token
+            for token in tokenizer.tokenize_str(text)
+            if tokenizer.is_special_token(token)
+        }
+        pattern = "|".join(re.escape(spelling) for spelling in special_tokens)
+        pieces = re.split(f"({pattern})", text) if special_tokens else [text]
+        return " ".join(
+            f"<[{special_tokens[piece]}]>"
+            if piece in special_tokens
+            else json.dumps(piece)
+            for piece in pieces
+            if piece
+        )
+
     def dispatch_structural_tag(self, key_string: str) -> BaseGrammarObject:
         try:
             structural_tag = json.loads(key_string)
             assert is_legacy_structural_tag(structural_tag)
             # Pair each structure with a trigger that prefixes its own
-            # ``begin`` — StructTag asserts begin.startswith(trigger), and
-            # detectors with per-tool triggers (e.g. Inkling's
+            # ``begin``. Detectors with per-tool triggers (e.g. Inkling's
             # <|message_model|>{name}<|content_invoke_tool_json|>) emit a
             # distinct trigger per tool, so triggers[0] matches only one of
             # them and multi-tool grammars fail to compile.
             triggers = structural_tag["triggers"]
-            tags = [
-                StructTag(
-                    begin=structure["begin"],
-                    grammar=structure["schema"],
-                    end=structure["end"],
-                    trigger=next(
-                        (t for t in triggers if structure["begin"].startswith(t)),
-                        triggers[0],
-                    ),
+            tags = []
+            for structure in structural_tag["structures"]:
+                begin = structure["begin"]
+                trigger = next(
+                    (t for t in triggers if begin.startswith(t)), triggers[0]
+                )
+                assert begin.startswith(trigger), "begin must start with trigger"
+                grammar = (
+                    f"start: {self._lark_literal(begin[len(trigger) :])} "
+                    f"%json {json.dumps(structure['schema'])} "
+                    f"{self._lark_literal(structure['end'])}"
+                )
+                tags.append(
+                    StructTag(begin=trigger, grammar=grammar, end="", trigger=trigger)
                 )
-                for structure in structural_tag["structures"]
-            ]
             g = StructTag.to_grammar(tags)
             return self._from_serialized(g)
         except Exception as e:

@@ -331,9 +331,12 @@ class TestLlguidanceStructuralTagTriggerPairing(unittest.TestCase):
     def test_each_structure_pairs_with_its_own_trigger(self):
         import json
 
+        from llguidance import LLTokenizer
+
         from sglang.srt.constrained.llguidance_backend import GuidanceBackend
 
         backend = object.__new__(GuidanceBackend)
+        backend.llguidance_tokenizer = LLTokenizer("byte")
         backend._from_serialized = lambda serialized: serialized
         begins = [
             '<|message_model|>alpha<|content_invoke_tool_json|>{"name":"alpha","args":',
@@ -360,6 +363,60 @@ def test_each_structure_pairs_with_its_own_trigger(self):
         self.assertNotIsInstance(result, InvalidGrammarObject)
 
 
+class TestLlguidanceStructuralTagSpecialTokens(unittest.TestCase):
+    """Bug regression: a structure's forced text spelled a special token, which
+    llguidance offered as the only allowed token and then rejected, so finishing
+    a tool call aborted the request with 'Grammar accept_token failed'."""
+
+    def test_forced_text_accepts_the_special_token_it_spells(self):
+        from llguidance.torch import allocate_token_bitmask
+        from tokenizers import Tokenizer, decoders, models, pre_tokenizers
+        from transformers import PreTrainedTokenizerFast
+
+        from sglang.srt.constrained.llguidance_backend import GuidanceBackend
+
+        alphabet = sorted(pre_tokenizers.ByteLevel.alphabet())
+        tokenizer = Tokenizer(
+            models.BPE(vocab={c: i for i, c in enumerate(alphabet)}, merges=[])
+        )
+        tokenizer.pre_tokenizer = pre_tokenizers.ByteLevel(add_prefix_space=False)
+        tokenizer.decoder = decoders.ByteLevel()
+        tokenizer.add_special_tokens(["<call>", "</call>", "<sep>", "<eos>"])
+        tokenizer = PreTrainedTokenizerFast(
+            tokenizer_object=tokenizer, eos_token="<eos>"
+        )
+        backend = GuidanceBackend(tokenizer, n_vocab=len(tokenizer))
+
+        for begin, end in (
+            ('<call>\n{"args":', "}\n</call>"),
+            ("<call>f<sep>", "</call>"),
+        ):
+            with self.subTest(begin=begin, end=end):
+                grammar = backend.dispatch_structural_tag(
+                    json.dumps(
+                        {
+                            "type": "structural_tag",
+                            "structures": [
+                                {
+                                    "begin": begin,
+                                    "schema": {"type": "object"},
+                                    "end": end,
+                                }
+                            ],
+                            "triggers": ["<call>"],
+                        }
+                    )
+                )
+                self.assertNotIsInstance(grammar, InvalidGrammarObject)
+
+                mask = allocate_token_bitmask(1, len(tokenizer))
+                call = begin + "{}" + end
+                for token in tokenizer.encode(call, add_special_tokens=False):
+                    grammar.fill_vocab_mask(mask, 0)
+                    self.assertTrue((int(mask[0, token // 32]) >> (token % 32)) & 1)
+                    grammar.accept_token(token)
+
+
 class TestNulByteGrammarRejection(unittest.TestCase):
     def setUp(self):
         self.backend = BaseGrammarBackend()
